name: Indigenous Herbal Teas (Thwngshwi)
ingredients: Fresh wild tea leaves (Camellia sinensis var. assamica)
instructions: 1. Bring water to a boil in a clay or earthen pot.
2. Crush the sun-dried ginger and black pepper into a coarse powder.
3. Add the tea leaves, crushed spices, lemongrass, and basil to the boiling water.
4. Reduce the heat and allow the mixture to simmer for 5-8 minutes until the infusion becomes fragrant and dark in color.
5. Strain the decoction into cups and stir in a small amount of jaggery if sweetness is desired.
description: Indigenous herbal teas, often consumed by the Tripuri and other tribal communities, are deeply rooted in traditional ethnomedicine. These teas are not just beverages but are served as health tonics to improve digestion, boost immunity, and combat seasonal illnesses, reflecting the intimate connection between the tribal forest dwellers and their biodiversity.
